# jochwacht-sbom 0.19.0 — send to your subscription, read more build files

- **`--send` sends the SBOM to your Jochwacht subscription.** The file written
  here goes as it is; the key comes from `JOCHWACHT_API_KEY`, never from the
  command line. Only https, no redirect is followed, the key is never printed
  or saved. Without a terminal (in a pipeline) it sends without a question
  and says so.
- **`jochwacht-sbom status`** reads the result of the version you sent:
  exit 0 for green, yellow or waiting for a person, 1 for red, 2 for an
  error or when the comparison still runs after `--wait`. It always prints
  the ready line of the answer.
- `--email`, `--voucher` and `--code` belonged to the free report, which is
  no longer offered; with `--send` they end with a message.
- CMake: libraries linked by their bare name (`target_link_libraries(fw z pq
  curl)`, `link_libraries`, `${VAR}`) are read; the project's own targets,
  imported targets, SDK targets and system libraries are not components.
- Autotools: `LIBS="$LIBS -l…"`, `*_LIBS` with `AC_SUBST` and `Makefile.am`
  (`fw_LDADD`) are read. In makefiles a `-l` name counts only on a line that
  links; `ls -lts` or `grep -lz` in a recipe is no library.
- Real libraries with a one- or two-character link name are kept (`-lz` is
  zlib, `-lpq` libpq); parts of the C library and the compiler runtime stay
  out on every path.
- Python requirements: a pin with hashes keeps its version, a comment line
  ends a continuation as in pip, and a lower bound or a range is no
  installed version.
- One size limit (64 MiB) for every reader; a skipped file is named.
- Names from the scanned project are text, never console markup; foreign
  text is cleaned of control and direction characters.
- The same library under several names is one component, under the name
  that leads to its key; different major versions (SDL and SDL2) stay apart.
